interest: Shows Japan's 1939 invitation of São Paulo professors, including a Rockefeller-linked hygienist, amid language-course and teacher surveillance.
overview: Despatches (1939): Japan invites five Brazilian professors, including two from São Paulo, on a paid Japan trip; Consul Foster also tracks weak Japanese-language enrollment and 47 registered Japanese teachers.

people.name: Carol H. Foster
people.role: American Consul General in São Paulo

people.name: Jefferson Caffery
people.role: American Ambassador to Brazil (Rio de Janeiro)

people.name: Junzo Sakané
people.role: Japanese Consul General in São Paulo

people.name: Geraldo de Paula Souza
people.role: Professor of the Faculty of Medicine, University of São Paulo; Head of the Institute of Hygiene

people.name: Soares de Mello
people.role: Professor of the Faculty of Law, University of São Paulo; Brazilian delegate to the Congress of Criminology in Rome

subfiles.about: Reports on a Japanese government initiative to invite five Brazilian university professors to Japan, as well as the status of Japanese language instruction and registered Japanese teachers in São Paulo.
subfiles.summary: Foster reports Japan's invitation for São Paulo professors to visit Japan, and weak enrollment in free Japanese-language courses.
subfiles.title: Letter from Consul General Foster to Ambassador Caffery on Japanese Propaganda and Invitation to Brazilian Professors

subfiles.about: Identifies the two professors from the University of São Paulo selected to visit Japan as guests of the Japanese government.
subfiles.summary: Foster names the two São Paulo professors selected for Japan's trip, including hygienist Dr. Paula Souza, tied to Rockefeller Foundation.
subfiles.title: Letter from Consul General Foster to Ambassador Caffery on Paulista Professors Invited to Japan
